abstention_composition.definition: skill = 1 - sum(Brier) / sum(base Brier) of the group's rows; the base rate is the trailing-window rate of the row's cell at its origin, the same number for every row of a stratum

inputs.decile_of: realized standard error s, pandas qcut into 10 bins

drift_matched_null.definition: drift-matched null: outcomes drawn with probability p_base (the trailing-window event rate of the row's cell at its origin), clustered by test; current null: outcomes drawn with the rung's own forecasts, clustered at the observed design effect (the report's null)

effect_scale_choices.definition: reversed means the 90 percent by-test interval of P1's pooled AUC for the significant-positive event lies below 0.5

absolute_realized.setting: absolute effect at realized precision (s_star changed alone)

cautionary.setting: relative lift at realized precision (the first run: both changes)

main.setting: absolute effect at planned precision (the default)

relative_planned.setting: relative lift at planned precision (effect scale changed alone)

effect_scale_choices.units: the relative runs score the relative lift in percent, so log scores and CRPS are not comparable across effect scales; the AUC, the Brier skill and the ECE are unitless and are

exposure_fixed.definition: every Upworthy row's two arms get the median planned exposure of its cell (admitted rows); y, s and the statuses are unchanged

gates_by_stratum.rule: decidable_by_tests: tests in the stratum against the stratum's own simulated n_200 and n_400 at the decision target (research screen beside)

inputs.in_selection_gain: mean per-row log-score gain over lambda 0 on the leave-one-test-out validation rows of the fit
inputs.unit: nats per row of log score

decomposition.definition: Both predictives are Student-t with the cell's degrees of freedom nu (P2 is moment matched in P1's family), so a row's log score is f(location, scale) = log of the density of theta + Normal(0, s_star^2) at y with theta ~ t(location, scale, nu). The difference f(loc2, sc2) - f(loc1, sc1) is split into a location part, the average of f(loc2, sc1) - f(loc1, sc1) and f(loc2, sc2) - f(loc1, sc2), and a scale part, the average of f(loc1, sc2) - f(loc1, sc1) and f(loc2, sc2) - f(loc2, sc1) (the two orders of changing one parameter at a time, averaged: the Shapley split of two players); the parts sum to the difference row by row. The locations and scales are those of the backtest's own predictives, refit at each admitted origin with the harness's factories and checked by recomputing both stored log scores.

inputs.decisive: the row's own realized |y| above z times its realized standard error (the harness's decisive rows)
inputs.difference: P2 log score minus P1 log score on the same row, nats; P2 better = difference above zero
inputs.event: the row's own realized y above z times its realized standard error (the significant-positive event)
inputs.intervals: percentile intervals by test from one set of resamples per pair (and one for the pooled rows); medians by weighted median
inputs.refit: P1 and P2 refit at each admitted origin with harness.default_rungs on ledger.visible_rows, the report's p2_guard

differences_from_docs: guard_admission_rates: the one-off runs behind the documentation left no report file, so the cells are refit here on ledgers regenerated with the same generator, text effect zero, 300 tests of two variants per seed; the seeds and the settings are in inputs

top_m_tail_share: the ledgers of 1e4 and 3e5 contrasts were not kept, so they are regenerated by benchmark.make_scale_ledger with the benchmark's seed; 1e5 reads the scale ledger when it exists; the 60 queries are drawn here with the seed in inputs
header.not_computed_reason: guard_admission_rates and top_m_tail_share are properties of the method on synthetic data and are in the synthetic source's report

inputs.exposure: mean of n_ref and n_var, natural log

inputs.null: clustered by test at the design effect of each origin's rows, as the main report draws it
inputs.rule: H3 part 1: the ECE of issued cards falls inside the central 90 percent of the null at most origins

inputs.definition: issued: abstain false; abstained: abstain true, scored on the forecast the rule withheld; each row set against its own base Brier
inputs.reading: pooled over origins and cells, so the composition of the two row sets (the burn-in origin and the event rate) is part of the difference

inputs.rule: H1 part 1: P1 beats P0 on log score at every origin after burn-in

p1_minus_p0_by_origin.unit: nats per row of log score, P1 minus P0

p2_selection_comparison.unit: nats per row of log score, forward chaining minus leave-one-test-out

prior_family_scale.definition: gains are maximized marginal log likelihoods of t minus normal, in nats, in sample; see the function docstring

randomization_window.notice: https://upworthy.natematias.com/about-the-archive (June 2024: evidence of randomization problems in about 22 percent of tests; causal or confirmatory use of tests from 25 June 2013 to 10 January 2014 is discouraged)

window.basis: UTC date of the earliest created_at of the test's packages

ranking_paired.definition: captured fraction = value captured by the K highest-ranked tests over the total value of the period (value = the best positive y among the test's contrasts), pooled over origins; s_star policy ranks tests by the smallest planned standard error of their contrasts (the most precise tests first, fixed before the run); s_star_desc is the opposite order (the least precise first), added beside it because the direction of an exposure-only policy was not specified by the plan

assurance_by_exposure.caveat: the planned exposure of an archive row is its realized impressions, a stand-in; X3 reports what fixing it at the cell median does

claim.note: regret differences are negative when the first rule costs less. A null is a result: it is reported as evaluated, not as not evaluated.
claim.verdict: evaluated; the prior rule's regret differs from a simpler rule's

test_and_roll.definition: relative regret = sum over units of (oracle gain - expected gain) over the sum of oracle gains, in the world of the rows scored at the origin and cell (nonparametric maximum likelihood effect distribution); sizes come from rows visible at the origin only
test_and_roll.horizon_note: N is a synthetic horizon in impressions, a multiple of the cell's test scale; there is no money. The nonparametric world is fitted to the rows scored at that origin and cell, so regret measures each rule against what happened later; the 0.67 and 1.5 worlds are printed beside the main one.

inputs.definition: rows abstained in the main run and issued in the run without the trigger
